page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the average tier for standard workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers average multi-core CPU performance with a stress-ng score of 7398.32 and a PassMark CPU score of 8292.45. Memory subsystem benchmarks show average read-only bandwidth of 413.79 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 50.27 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the lower tier, indicating potential performance limitations under highly parallelized compute-intensive tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-8 offers a standard resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average performance in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, this instance is appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, application hosting, software development builds, and moderate database operations.
